title: Welch learns guitar from country suppers and juke-house pianists
summary: Welch learned guitar at his mother's country suppers and from piano players in juke houses.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, maybe we'd better turn it off now. Yes. All right. I'd like to record your record again. Now, uh. We just did get you born. I know something's happened since then. Yes, sir. You must have started out in music some way. Did any of your family play?
Well, uh, not exactly. Now, people didn't play, but my mother and them always used to give country ball, what you might call a country supper.

And the guitar players would leave their guitar at our house until the next day. Mm-hmm. Well, I'd be plowing out in the field. I'd plow till my mule would get hot. I'd let them cool off and run to the house and practice a little bit on the guitar and just kept on that way until I learned a note or two. And when I learned a note or two, I came to town and stopped around those juke houses around there where they play piano and things. Mm-hmm. And I was taking the guitar and asked the piano player, would he mind me trying to learn a little bit? Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. He showed me. I mean, he played his piano, and I just felt the music and felt the notes. Okay. Until I found the notes. And when I found the notes, well, there I was.
Well, who were the piano players?
A boy called Dollar Bar. Dollar Bar. Yes, sir. He's a nine-finger fellow. He stayed in Vicksburg, Mississippi. He's an old, resident piano player.
